messages.subject: posterior correrlation
parts:
Dear Group,

I tried to estimate posterior correlations using lincombs, but ran into random numerical problems.

Please advise the attached examples.

set.seed(7)
n = 100
nPred = 10

phi = 0.9
x = arima.sim(n,  model = list(ar=phi)) * sqrt(1-phi^2)
y = 1 + x + rnorm(n,  sd=0.1)

time = 1:(n + nPred)
Y = c(y, rep(NA, nPred))
formula = Y ~ 1 + f(time, model="rw1")

## make linear combinations which are the nPred linear predictors
B = matrix(NA, n, n+nPred)
for(i in 1:n) {
    B[i, i] = 1
}
lcs = inla.make.lincombs(time = B)

r = inla(formula,  data = data.frame(Y, time),
        control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE),
        lincomb = lcs,
        control.inla = list(lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix=TRUE))

print(b<-r$misc$lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix)

Regards

Dong Liang

> print(b<-r$misc$lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix)

Hi,

I'm not sure what you mean here. you simulate using an AR1 and estimate
using an RW1, note that RW1 has default constr=TRUE, so this means that
all of them are posterior correlated (really non-zero...). so if you
change the formula into

Y ~ -1 + f(time, model="rw1", constr=FALSE)

you'll get very different results. maybe this is what is confusing.

I attach an edited version of the code, for which the posterior
correlation matrix is know to that of an AR1 and then I do a comparison
using fixed hyperparameters.

Best
H


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

Hi,

Many thanks for clearing my confusions.
Please see following the code corrected by  Håvard Rue. Errors are in the comments.

library(INLA)
 set.seed(7)
 n = 10
 nPred = 5

phi = 0.9
 x = arima.sim(n,  model = list(ar=phi)) * sqrt(1-phi^2)

s = 0.1
 y = x + rnorm(n,  sd=s)
## Error 1 ###
## y = 1 + x + rnorm(n, sd=s)
## sum-to-zero constraints changed the posterior correlation matrix,no longer AR1
###############

time = 1:(n + nPred)
 Y = c(y, rep(NA, nPred))

formula = Y ~ -1 + f(time, model="ar1",constr=FALSE,
                    hyper=list(prec=list(initial=0,fixed=TRUE),
                            rho=list(initial=log((1+phi)/(1-phi)), fixed=TRUE))) 
## Error 1 ###
# formula = Y ~ 1 + f(time, model="ar1",constr=TRUE,
#                    hyper=list(prec=list(initial=0,fixed=TRUE),
#                            rho=list(initial=log((1+phi)/(1-phi)), fixed=TRUE))) 
###############
 
 ## make linear combinations which are the n linear predictors

B = matrix(NA, n, n+nPred)
 for(i in 1:n) {
     B[i, i] = 1
 }
 lcs = inla.make.lincombs(time = B)
 
 r = inla(formula,  data = data.frame(Y, time),
         control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE),

control.family = list(hyper = list(
                                      prec = list(
                                              initial = log(1/s^2),
                                              fixed=TRUE))),
